summary: Defines a new email header field, Archived-At, that gives a direct link to the archived copy of a particular message. It is useful for mailing lists that keep web archives, so recipients can link straight to the message. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Every letter gets a note on it saying where a copy is filed in the library. You can follow the note to find that exact letter again.

questions: how to link to an archived email message
how to link to an archived email
subtitle: An email header that points straight to the archived copy of that one message.

tldr.problem: Mailing list headers could point to the archive as a whole, but there was no standard way to point to the archived copy of a single message.
tldr.mechanism: A new header field, Archived-At, holds one URI in angle brackets that locates the archived form of the message. Several archive locations mean several header fields.
tldr.outcome: Readers and software can jump from a message to its archive entry and to related messages. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no replacement.

today: RFC 5064 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2007, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Per-Message Archive Link
sections.content:
RFC 2369 defines header fields for list messages, including List-Archive, which describes how to reach the archives of a list as a whole. It does not point to an individual message.

RFC 5064 adds the Archived-At header field to refer to a single message at an archived location. It gives quick access to a mailing list message in the list archive, and it can also be used without mailing lists, for example for legal requirements to archive certain messages.
sections.eli5: A sign saying where the whole library is does not help you find one letter. This note says which shelf holds your exact letter.

sections.title: Header Field Syntax
sections.content:
The field name is Archived-At. The field body is one URI enclosed in angle brackets. The URI may contain folding whitespace, which is ignored. Mail Transfer Agents MUST NOT insert whitespace within the angle brackets, but client applications SHOULD ignore any whitespace that poorly behaved MTAs inserted.

The RFC gives the grammar in ABNF: archived-at = "Archived-At:" [FWS] "<" folded-URI ">" CRLF. To turn a folded URI into a URI, apply the standard unfolding rules and then delete any remaining un-encoded space characters.

The syntax is kept simple: only one URI per field is allowed, and comments are not allowed. In this it differs from RFC 2369.
sections.eli5: The note holds exactly one address, written between two angle brackets. If a printer splits the address across lines, you glue it back together.

sections.title: Multiple Fields, Fragments and Forwarding
sections.content:
To list several places where an archived copy can be found, use one Archived-At field per URI. Fields with the same URI SHOULD be avoided, and a field SHOULD only be created if the message is actually available at that URI.

When a list forwards a message to a sublist and both add the field, the sublist SHOULD add a new field without removing existing ones. If the new field is exactly the same as an existing one, it SHOULD NOT be added.

For MIME message fragmentation and reassembly, Archived-At is treated like Comments: copied to the first fragment and back to the reassembled message. Because of this, the field in the first fragment MAY refer to the whole unfragmented message, and the field SHOULD NOT be added to fragment messages.

Where non-ASCII text is allowed directly in header fields, the URI is replaced by an Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) as defined in RFC 3987.
sections.eli5: If a letter is filed in three libraries, it gets three notes, one for each. A second library adds its own note without crossing out the first.

sections.title: Archive Formats, Usage and Implementation
sections.content:
There is no restriction on the format served from the URI. The RFC expects (X)HTML, plain text, or the original message/rfc822 form. If the retrieval protocol supports content negotiation, an HTTP URI could serve text/html to a browser and message/rfc822 to a mail client.

Mailing list software and archives are often separate, so creating the field in the list software can be hard. One approach is to generate an unambiguous URI from the message identifier of the incoming email and have the archive redirect requests for it to the real message. If there is no message identifier, a unique one can be generated. The RFC describes such a system in use at W3C. Characters not allowed in a URI must be escaped or removed.

The RFC lists uses for the pointer: referring to a message outside email, such as on a Web page or in a phone conversation; pointing to several messages in a message; and finding related messages in the archive. Mostly a human reader uses the URI, though software may too.
sections.eli5: The note can lead to a web page, a plain text copy or the original letter. It helps when you want to tell a friend exactly which letter you mean.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Activating a URI carries general risks covered by the URI specification. Two are called out: an intruder who can reach message transmission could insert a URI pointing to malicious content, which a secured transmission path addresses; and a message harmless on arrival could cause problems through the archive if the archive format did not escape content properly.

A denial-of-service risk exists because the archived copy may itself contain an Archived-At field. If software downloads archived copies automatically and follows URIs recursively without checking for repeats, it can hammer the server. The RFC says the URI should not be dereferenced automatically and that loop detection should be used.

Also, someone could reuse a message identifier to break the link to a message. Countermeasures include rejecting duplicate identifiers, discarding significantly different duplicates, offering several choices in the response, or authenticating incoming messages.
sections.eli5: Do not blindly follow every note, or you could end up running in circles. Check that the shelf really holds the right letter.

sections.title: The X-Archived-At Precursor and IANA
sections.content:
For backwards compatibility the RFC also describes X-Archived-At, an earlier form. It MAY be parsed but SHOULD not be generated. Its syntax is "X-Archived-At:" SP URI CRLF, with no whitespace allowed inside the URI.

IANA registered Archived-At in the Message Header Fields Registry with status standard, for mail and netnews, with the IETF as change controller. X-Archived-At is registered with status deprecated.
sections.eli5: There was an older kind of sticker with a slightly different name. New letters should use the new name, but old stickers can still be read.
